answer_summary: R Equation for CO₂ scrubbing by the aqueous solution of compound 3 (N-methyldiethanolamine, MDEA, a tertiary amine, so carbonation goes to bicarbonate, not carbamate): CH3N(CH2CH2OH)2 + CO2 + H2O -> [CH3NH(CH2CH2OH)2]+ + HCO3-, i.e. C5H13NO2 + CO2 + H2O -> [C5H14NO2]+ + [HCO3]-. All stoichiometric coefficients are 1; the equation is element-balanced (C:6=6, H:15=15, N:1=1, O:5=5) and charge-balanced (0 = +1 + -1).
assumptions: Compound 3 is N-methyldiethanolamine MeN(CH2CH2OH)2 (C5H13NO2), read directly off the structure printed on official page Q7-2.

The reaction asked for is the CO2-scrubbing reaction: problem text 'An aqueous solution of 3 is being used to remove CO2 from the mixture.' (Q7-2, immediately above box 7.4; box Z is labeled 'CO2 scrubber' in Fig. 1 on Q7-1).

Trusted general law (allowed by the candidate domain policy): a tertiary amine such as MDEA has no N-H proton and therefore absorbs CO2 in water as the ammonium hydrogen-carbonate pair R3NH+ HCO3- rather than as a carbamate.

Formalization level: species are modeled by molecular formulas (strings) with their elemental compositions (C,H,N,O) and net charges; the CRNT Reaction structure models the chemical equation. No molecular-graph model is required for a requested output of kind 'chemical-equation'.
